PM Vishwakarma Beneficiaries Invited as ‘Special Guests’ to Witness 80th Independence Day Ceremony at Red Fort, Delhi
articles.full_content:
100 beneficiaries from Delhi-NCR to attend the Celebration
The Government of India has invited 100 beneficiaries of PM Vishwakarma from the Delhi-NCR region as ‘Special Guests’ to witness the 80th Independence Day Ceremony at the Red Fort, Delhi, on 15th August, 2026. The beneficiaries will attend the national celebration along with their spouse/companion.
The Special Guests also include women artisans from various traditional trades, reflecting the scheme’s contribution towards women’s economic empowerment, greater participation in livelihoods and strengthening the role of women in preserving India’s rich artisanal and cultural heritage.
Recognition and Appreciation of Beneficiaries- As part of their participation, the PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries will also be presented with souvenirs as a token of recognition and appreciation, followed by an interaction with officials of the Ministry of MSME on 14 August 2026 at the Indian Institute of Public Administration, Delhi, recognising their contribution to India’s traditional crafts and cultural heritage.
About PM Vishwakarma Scheme-
PM Vishwakarma is one of the flagship initiatives of the Government of India aimed at providing comprehensive support to artisans and craftspeople engaged in traditional trades. The scheme provides assistance through skill upgradation, modern tools, financial support, digital enablement and market linkages, with the objective of promoting the socio-economic empowerment of artisans, strengthening traditional crafts and ensuring sustainable livelihoods. Under the scheme, 30 lakh traditional artisans and craftspeople have been registered.
Celebrating the Contribution of India’s Traditional Artisans & Craftspeople
The invited beneficiaries represent the 18 traditional trades covered under PM Vishwakarma, including Tailor, Carpenter, Goldsmith, Blacksmith, Locksmith, among others. The beneficiaries invited have availed various benefits under the scheme, including registration, Basic Skill Training and provision of toolkits, along with other support benefits available under the scheme.
The participation of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries in the Independence Day celebration is recognition of the invaluable contribution of traditional artisans and craftspeople to India’s rich cultural heritage. Their presence at the Red Fort will provide them an opportunity to witness the grandeur of the 80th Independence Day and to be a part of this historic national celebration.

STP Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme to promote software and IT-enabled services (IT/ITeS) exports from India and STPI has been providing Statutory Services on a single-window Clearance System under STP Scheme.

Measures taken by the Software technology Parks of India (STPI) to streamline approvals and improve ease of doing business for STP units are as follows:
• Automation of Statutory Services: For providing seamless services to the IT exporters, statutory services including SOFTEX filling, its approval and final intimation to them has been automated. This has ensured speedy delivery of services to the satisfaction of the IT industry.
• Integration with RBI’s Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) System for IT exporters: STPI’s online system for IT exporters has been integrated with the Reserve Bank of India’s EDPMS for sharing of export data. This integration has enabled seamless electronic transmission of export declaration data to RBI in near real time. This has facilitated faster exchange of export data, enhanced accuracy and transparency, reduced manual intervention, improved monitoring of export transactions, and streamlined regulatory compliance for IT/ITeS exporters.

• Self-Declaration for Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) Sales: The requirement for prior DTA permissions for STPI-registered units has been replaced with a submission of self-declaration (except for advance DTA sales in first year of operation).

EPFO REGIONAL OFFICE, MYSURU LAUNCHES “EMPLOYEES’ ENROLMENT CAMPAIGN (EEC) 2026” TO EXPAND SOCIAL SECURITY COVERAGE
articles.full_content:
The Employees' Provident Fund Organization (EPFO), Regional Office, Mysuru, has formally launched the Employees' Enrolment Campaign (EEC), 2026. This special one-time compliance facilitation drive aims to extend statutory social security coverage to eligible employees while encouraging voluntary compliance among employers across the region. The initiative will remain active for a limited period until October 31, 2026.
Under this campaign, employers are enabled to voluntarily enroll eligible employees, who remained outside EPF coverage between April 1, 2009, and March 31, 2026, thereby extending statutory social security benefits while promoting voluntary compliance under the EPF & MP Act. To facilitate smooth participation, the campaign offers significant compliance relief to employers. Where the employee's share of the EPF contribution was not deducted from wages, the same shall be completely waived, requiring employers to remit only the employer's share of contribution alongside applicable interest, administrative charges, and a nominal damage fee of ₹100. Overall, the initiative seeks to expand social security coverage and foster formal employment in the region.
To participate, employers are required to complete the enrolment process digitally through the EPFO Employer Portal using the dedicated EEC-2026 module. The streamlined online process includes submitting a digital declaration, generating Universal Account Numbers (UAN) via Face Authentication technology, filing the Electronic Challan cum Return (ECR), and completing the digital submission of all required declarations.
Highlighting the scope and significance of the campaign, the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Mysuru, stated that the Employees' Enrolment Campaign provides employers with a unique opportunity to regularize eligible employees while extending essential provident fund, pension, and insurance benefits to them. The Commissioner urged all eligible establishments across the region to avail themselves of the scheme before the final deadline of October 31, 2026.
To ensure seamless implementation and assist establishments in completing the enrolment process, EPFO Mysuru has been actively conducting awareness programmes, employer outreach meetings, and stakeholder interactions throughout the region. Employers seeking further information or assistance are encouraged to visit the official EPFO Employer Portal or directly contact the EPFO Regional Office in Mysuru.

Colourful coral display sparks curiosity, offers insights on climate adaptation research
articles.full_content:
Indication of both resilience and vulnerability to climate stress, says CMFRI
Kochi: In an intriguing spectacle of marine life, a natural coral assemblage in tricolour beneath the sea has sparked curiosity and offered critical insights on climate adaptation research.
The underwater image captured during a marine mammal survey by the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) from Minicoy, Lakshadweep shows two coral colonies appearing in tricolour—orange, white and green— come together naturally.
The species were identified as Lobophyllia corymbose with its vibrant orange colour, and Lobophyllia radians in white and green colours.
Captured by CMFRI Research Scholar Alvin Anto, the underwater image provides valuable insights on the contrasting response of corals to environmental stress. While one L. radians colony underwent bleaching after losing its symbiotic algae, its neighbouring colony remains healthy despite growing in close proximity.
Resilience and Vulnerability “Though this assemblage is a symbol of India's rich marine biodiversity, it also carries an urgent message about ocean health. It tells the stark story of resilience and vulnerability to climate stress. While one colony of coral species bleached due to rising sea temperatures, its direct neighbour of the same species remains healthy and green. This variation in thermal stress tolerance offers crucial insights for the ongoing reef restoration and climate adaptation research”, said CMFRI Director Dr Grinson George.
Reef Restoration Emphasising the urgent need to tackle these climate impacts, he highlighted measures being taken up by the CMFRI towards coral reef restoration. “With the support from the Government of India, CMFRI is on a mission to rapidly scale up the deployment of Artificial Reefs along coastal waters to revive degraded habitats, enhance coastal biodiversity, and support the livelihoods of artisanal fishers”, he added.
Simultaneously, efforts are underway to replenish depleted wild stocks of ecologically and economically vital marine species through marine fish breeding, seed production, and sea ranching programmes, Dr George said. Restoring natural habitats through artificial reefs is expected to support marine ecosystems and build a robust climate resilient marine ecosystem, he said, adding that this coral assemblage serves as a reminder to safeguard the fragile coral ecosystems in a warming world.

As the nation prepares to celebrate the 80 th Independence Day, Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) , the flagship rural drinking water programme of the Government of India, is set to complete seven years of transformative progress in improving the lives of rural households across the country. Launched by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 15 August 2019, Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide every rural household with safe and adequate drinking water through a Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) on a regular and long-term basis.
At the time of the launch of the Mission, only 3.23 crore rural households, representing about 16.72% of rural households in the country, had tap water connections. Today more than 15.91 crore rural households have tap water supply in their homes, accounting for 82.24% of all rural households. Since the launch of the Mission, over 12.68 crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections, significantly improving access to safe drinking water across rural India.

The same can be publicly viewed real-time on the Jal Jeevan Mission- Integrated Management Information System (JJM-IMIS) portal https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx
Rural drinking water supply has been a national development priority since Independence. Over the decades, successive initiatives including the National Water Supply Programme (1954), Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme (1972-73), National Drinking Water Mission (1986), Swajaldhara (2002) and the National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP) contributed significantly to expanding access to safe drinking water in rural areas. These programmes laid the foundation for strengthening rural water infrastructure and addressing water quality and sustainability challenges. Building upon these efforts, Jal Jeevan Mission marked a paradigm shift from habitation-level coverage to service delivery at the household level through Functional Household Tap Connections, with a focus on adequate quantity (55 lpcd.) of prescribed quality (BIS:10500) on regular and long-term basis at affordable service delivery charges leading to improvement in living standards of rural communities.

Consultation focuses on ESDP, Japanese language training, employer linkages and industry-led skilling

The consultation focused on taking forward the Action Plan for India-Japan Human Resource Exchange and Cooperation, jointly released during the 15th India-Japan Annual Summit in 2025. Discussions centred on preparing Indian youth for employment opportunities in Japan through industry-relevant training, Japanese language and cultural preparation, recognised assessments, stronger employer engagement and closer coordination among institutions in both countries.

articles.title: NITI Aayog releases report on India’s Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services
articles.full_content:
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, launched the third report under the Services Thematic Series at the forum of the High-Powered ‘Education to Employment and Enterprise’ Standing Committee, in the presence of Smt. Nidhi Chhibber, CEO, NITI Aayog, and Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MOSPI, on 10th August 2026. The launch was attended by senior officers from the Ministries/Departments, State Governments, Industry Associations, and Experts/Academia, who are members of the High-Powered Committee.
The report, “ India’s Services Sector: Insights on Regulatory Regime in Professional Services ”, presents a unique factual assessment of India’s regulatory framework in professional services and benchmarks it against select foreign jurisdictions. Drawing on extensive stakeholder consultations, it also identifies key challenges and outlines a way forward to strengthen the sector and unlock the full potential of India’s professional workforce.
Professional services is a key sub-sector in the services economy, accounting for nearly a quarter of India’s total services exports. As high-value, knowledge-intensive activities, they enable efficient delivery of downstream services, support job creation and remittance inflows, and form the backbone of the services value chain. Understanding the regulatory ecosystem governing these services is therefore critical to unlocking further growth.
The report adopts a balanced approach and provides sector-specific insights, alongside a four-pronged strategy to enhance the efficiency and output of professional services: harnessing emerging trends to transform professional services; elevate professional services within the services value chain; adoption of best practices in professional services, and continuous professional development for professionals.
As India approaches its demographic peak, professional services oﬀer significant opportunities for high-skilled employment, entrepreneurship and innovation. A well-designed regulatory ecosystem can further strengthen service exports, cross-border mobility of professionals and the ease of doing business.
The report provides an indicative pathway for future policy dialogue and deeper examination of the regulatory foundations of professional services. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat @2047, such eﬀorts will be integral to building a globally competitive, inclusive and future-ready services sector.

As part of the Independence Day celebrations, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Government of India, organized the PMIS Industry Awards on August 14, 2026, in New Delhi to recognize the contribution of partner companies in the successful implementation of the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) during its pilot phase.
The event was chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and was attended by senior officials of the Ministry, representatives from leading industry partners, and more than 100 current and former PMIS interns from across the country.

Mahindra & Mahindra Limited was recognized as the Overall Industry Champion for its leadership and exemplary contribution to promoting internships and youth engagement under PMIS.

A representative from Mahindra & Mahindra Limited said, “Today, we have crossed the milestone of welcoming 1,000 interns across the Mahindra Group.

The example reflected the Scheme’s potential not only to provide workplace exposure but also to support higher education and long-term career growth.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) continuously monitors weather and climate across the country, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu, through its observational networks and numerical weather prediction models. Key climate and risk assessments conducted by MoES institutes include the regular preparation of Monthly and Annual Climate Summaries, State-wise Climate Statements, and Climate Diagnostic Bulletins, which document regional, state, and district-level climate variations, including extreme temperatures, heatwaves, cold waves, and rainfall variability over the past 30 years.
The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) maintains the Ocean Moored Network for the Northern Indian Ocean (OMNI), coastal buoys, High-Frequency (HF) Radars, and Tsunami buoys in the Indian Ocean region, including two buoys in the Arabian Sea, to monitor real-time meteorological and oceanographic parameters.
The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) has prepared a Coastal Vulnerability Index (CVI) at a scale of 1:100,000 for the entire Indian coastline, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu, considering factors such as sea-level rise, shoreline changes, and tidal dynamics. In addition, Coastal Multi-Hazard Vulnerability Mapping (MHVM) has been carried out at a scale of 1:25,000 to support coastal risk assessment and disaster preparedness.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) operates a nationwide observational network comprising Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs), Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs), and rain gauge stations for district- and block-level weather monitoring.
The Ministry of Earth Sciences, through the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), maintains dedicated coastal High Frequency (HF) Radar pairs, including those at Wasiborsi and Jegri in Gujarat, along with a network of open-ocean moored buoys for continuous ocean observations. The National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR) provides urban rainfall forecasts and flood inundation mapping covering approximately 400 sq. km of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation area to support urban flood management.
Weather warnings and alerts are disseminated through multiple digital platforms, including the MAUSAM, Meghdoot, DAMINI, UMANG, and SAMUDRA mobile applications, as well as the SACHET platform based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP), ensuring timely last-mile dissemination.
Real-time data generated from oceanic and meteorological observation networks are assimilated into high-resolution operational oceanic and atmospheric models to enhance forecasting accuracy and support disaster risk reduction.

Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the scheme Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri Janjati Maha Nyaya Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) through Tribal Co-operative Marketing Development Federation (TRIFED) to facilitate and promote livelihood opportunities and entrepreneurship in the tribal population through establishment of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs). During the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26), 617 VDVKs have been sanctioned under PMJVM and 540 VDVKs under PM JANMAN across various States/ UTs. Through these VDVKs, support has been provided for skill development, capacity building, value addition, processing, plantation, and marketing assistance, alongside the creation of self-employment opportunities and livelihood enhancement.
Additionally, National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE), provides concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe persons for undertaking income generation, self-employment and livelihood activities. In the last five years, NSTFDC has disbursed loans amounting to ₹1648.39 cr to 4,95,090 ST beneficiaries under its various schemes.

NITI Aayog has released the report titled “ Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub ”, which through a structured and data-driven framework identifies major sectors that can fuel India’s ambition to become global manufacturing powerhouse. It also examines the factors that influence manufacturing competitiveness, including market potential, infrastructure readiness, policy support, raw material availability, technology readiness, employment potential and India’s current position in the value chain.
The project seeks to identify sectors where India has significant growth potential and where targeted interventions can strengthen domestic capabilities, enhance competitiveness and value addition, and accelerate export-oriented manufacturing growth. The study also draws on the experience of leading manufacturing countries to develop sector-specific recommendations for addressing key challenges and promoting growth in the identified sectors.

As per the SBM(G) Phase-II guidelines, various interventions can be undertaken for GWM such as constructions of soak-pit, leach-pit, magic-pit or kitchen garden at household level and Waste Stabilization Ponds, Constructed Wetland, Decentralized Wastewater Treatment System (DEWATS) and Phytorid Technology at community/village level. The SBM(G) IMIS does not capture details of category-wise rural drains (for example: open, closed, kutcha, or pucca drain) or unconnected or inadequate open drains.

articles.full_content:
Sujal Gaon and Sujalam Bharat IDs Strengthen Digital Governance of Rural Water Supply Under JJM
The Sujal Gaon ID is a unique identification number assigned under the digital monitoring framework of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 for water supply service area (habitation/s) meeting the prescribed standards and criteria under the Mission. The ID is issued through the national JJM digital platform and the details are communicated to the respective States/UTs through the JJM digital ecosystem. The objective of the Sujal Gaon ID is to facilitate systematic identification, monitoring, reporting, tracking and verification of water supply service area (habitation/s) achieving desired outcomes in rural drinking water service delivery and sustainability. As on 10.08.2026, out of 16,96,213 habitations in the country, Sujal Gaon IDs have been issued to 12,67,808 habitations (75%) across all States/UTs.
Sujalam Bharat has been developed as a federated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) for lifecycle-based and service-oriented management of Rural Piped Water Supply Schemes (RPWSS). It integrates digital asset registries, geospatial mapping and decision-support systems to provide unified visibility of water supply infrastructure. Integrated with the PM GatiShakti platform, it provides a GIS-validated architecture and assigns unique digital identities to rural water supply schemes through Sujalam Bharat IDs.
Sujal Gaon IDs and Sujalam Bharat IDs under the Jal Jeevan Mission provide unique digital identities to service areas and rural water supply schemes, respectively. Their integration with GIS and structured hydraulic linkages enables end-to-end source-to-tap mapping, asset tracking and lifecycle management. This facilitates better planning, monitoring and accountability of existing schemes, helps identify gaps and duplication, and enables data-driven decision-making and effective Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Thus, these digital IDs strengthen transparency and oversight and help reduce irregularities in the implementation of JJM.
This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI V. SOMANNA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

NITI Aayog has released the report titled “ Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub ”, which through a structured and data-driven framework identifies major sectors that can fuel India’s ambition to become global manufacturing powerhouse. The project seeks to identify sectors where India has significant growth potential and where targeted interventions can strengthen domestic capabilities, enhance competitiveness and value addition, and accelerate export-oriented manufacturing growth. The study also draws on the experience of leading manufacturing countries to develop sector-specific recommendations for addressing key challenges and promoting growth in the identified sectors.

Phase 1: Shortlisting Sectors Based on Relative Attractiveness: Identification of sectors with high growth potential based on market size and growth prospects in both domestic and global markets.

Phase 3: Benchmarking International Best Practices: Analyses of best practices and successful approaches adopted by top performing countries to identify relevant strategies and lessons for India’s shortlisted sectors.

articles.full_content:
India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) comprises of three quantitative targets namely the reduction of overall emissions intensity of our Gross Domestic Product (GDP), enhancing share of non-fossil fuel-based energy resources in installed electric power capacity and creation of additional carbon sink.
India had achieved a reduction of 37.38% in the emissions intensity of its GDP in 2022 from the 2005 level, against the NDC goal of reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030. The share of cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy sources crossed 50% in June 2025, thereby achieving the NDC goal five years ahead of the committed timeline. As of 30th June 2026, non-fossil fuel-based energy resources accounted for 54.18% of the country’s total installed electric power capacity. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005 to 2022, against the NDC goal of creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2030 through additional forest and tree cover.
As reported in India’s first Biennial Transparency Report submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in April, 2026, the decoupling of greenhouse gas emissions from economic growth and GDP can be attributed to policies promoting renewable energy deployment, improving the energy efficiency of all economic activity. The early achievement of NDC goal on share of non-fossil fuel based installed electric power capacity has been made possible by a range of policies that incentivize renewable energy generation and its integration in to national electricity grid. The creation of carbon sink could be possible because of high priority accorded to conservation and restoration by the national and the State governments. The approach is reflected in the framework of Policies, Acts, Rules, Programmes and Schemes to ensure conservation of forests and biodiversity, enhance green cover and participation of people in the conservation activities while protecting rights of forest dependent communities.
The NDC targets for the year 2035 have been enhanced, with quantitative targets to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% from the 2005 level, achieve 60% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources, and create carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest and tree cover as compared to the baseline year of
2005. The NDC also includes five qualitative targets aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyles, enhancing adaptation capacity and adoption of climate friendly cleaner path aligned with the goal of Viksit Bharat @2047.

articles.full_content:
Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including the state of Kerala. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills. Some of the key schemes under SIM are:
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY): The PMKVY Scheme is for imparting skill development training through Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to youth across the country including the state of Kerala.
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme : The scheme aims to impart vocational skills to the non-literates, neo-literates and the persons having a rudimentary level of education and school dropouts up to 12th standard in the age group of 15-45 years, with due age relaxation in case of “Divyangjan” and other deserving cases. Priority is given to Women, SC, ST, OBC and Minorities in the rural areas and urban low-income areas.
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS): This Scheme is for promoting apprenticeship training and increasing the engagement of apprentices by providing financial support for payment of stipend to apprentices. Training consists of Basic Training and On-the- Job Training / Practical Training at the workplace in the industry.
Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS): This scheme is for providing long-term training through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across the country. The ITIs offer a range of vocational/skill training courses covering many economic sectors with the objective to provide a skilled workforce to the industry as well as self-employment of youth.

National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services
articles.full_content:
The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) today launched its e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services. Hon’ble President, NCLT, Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, inaugurated the services through video conferencing, marking another step towards making the Tribunal’s Registry more accessible and technology-enabled.
Speaking on the occasion, Justice Grewal said that the two services are intended to provide advocates, litigants and other stakeholders with convenient and faster access to judicial records and certified copies. The services form part of the Tribunal’s broader digital transformation, including the revamped NCLT website and the ongoing e-Courts 2.0 initiative.
The Hon’ble NCLT President also highlighted the measures undertaken to improve case management and reduce pendency. The NCLT has adopted a data-driven mechanism to monitor pendency across Benches. Based on the data so collated, workload was reviewed and redistributed, Special Benches were constituted wherever required, and efforts were made to maximise the available Court time.
These measures contributed to the approval of 78 resolution plans during April–June 2026, the highest first-quarter performance since the enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, involving approximately ₹5,517.66 crore.
The NCLT has also issued detailed guidelines on registration and listing of cases, in consultation with the Bar, to ensure optimum utilisation of limited judicial resources.
Justice Grewal emphasised that while the Tribunal continues to face infrastructural and manpower constraints, sustained efforts are being made to reduce avoidable delays and improve efficiency.
The launch of the two services is part of the NCLT’s continuing endeavour to provide a more transparent, efficient and stakeholder-oriented system of justice delivery.

Partnership to Enable Voice-First, Multilingual AI for Citizen-Centric Governance and Public Service Delivery
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) , under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and NITI Aayog , Government of India, have signed a Statement of Intent (SoI) to collaborate on advancing multilingual, voice-first AI solutions for inclusive governance and citizen-centric public service delivery through the BHASHINI for Seva/Sanchalan initiative.
The SoI was signed by Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division , and Shri Shoyabahmed Kalal, Director, NITI Aayog .
The collaboration aims to leverage BHASHINI's multilingual AI ecosystem to enable more inclusive and accessible governance by integrating AI-powered language technologies across NITI Aayog's digital platforms and services. The partnership will facilitate access to government information and services in citizens' preferred Indian languages, strengthen communication between government and citizens, and promote multilingual operations across public service delivery.
Under the SoI, both organisations will collaborate across BHASHINI Udyat, BHASHINI Mitra, BHASHINI AppMitra, BHASHINI Sahayogi and BHASHINI Pravakta . The partnership will facilitate multilingual access to NITI Aayog services through BHASHINI's language translation APIs and reference applications, support the development and continuous improvement of translation models, and enable the integration of language technologies into digital platforms, document management systems and communication workflows.
The collaboration will also support the development of reference applications and voice bots for specific NITI Aayog sectors and strengthen language technology for specialised terminology and sector-specific requirements. Through BHASHINI Sahayogi , the partnership will leverage BhashaDaan for the collection, curation and dissemination of linguistic data, with NITI Aayog officials and citizens encouraged to contribute text, audio and video samples.
Through BHASHINI Pravakta , the two organisations will work towards expanding awareness and adoption of BHASHINI's services, tools and resources across districts, supported by training, technical assistance and resources to ensure that multilingual digital solutions remain accessible to users with varying levels of digital literacy.
The collaboration also builds on NITI TARA (Toolkit for Analysis, Review & Action) , which is transforming data into action at the grassroots. With 200+ capacity-building sessions conducted across the country, NITI TARA has empowered over 4,000 officials from districts and blocks to leverage data-driven insights for evidence-based decision-making.
